	Re: Heppy Naw Xmas
	
	
	
	
	

I believe that the best way to beat shyness is to be in a safe environment. By 
surrounding yourself with things that make you feel comfortable/desired, you 
should find your feeling of anxiety are reduced. As you experience this more, 
you will come to realise that you do not need to feel shy any more.
This process may take some time however. I would suggest that you start with an 
enclosed environment that makes you feel warm and safe.. somewhere soft and 
relaxing, maybe with candles and soft music. When you feel more comfortable 
with yourself, take the time to imagine how you would see yourself from 
"outside" - maybe a mirror. Again, take your time and when you feel really 
comfortable with this, only then should you start to seek outside opinion. You 
should start with people you are reasonably sure will express themselves in 
positive appreciation of you before moving onto more hostile people. (like me!)
Private lessons are cheaper, as there is more of me to go... ;)
x

We are pleased to inform you that, as usual, you have been provided with a wide 
selection of reasons for working at DDS (as listed below). Please take the time 
to peruse this list and ponder on how lucky you are to work for one of the 
foremost advertising medium purchasing,buying and billing companies in the 
whole wide world:
1) Unlike other companies, DDS does not focus on a reward/achievement model, we 
at DDS work on the honour system which requires no reward beyond the personal 
satisfaction of doing a job well.
1) In a bold and adventurous move, DDS has taken a departmentalised 
staff-rotation model where high staff turnover is focused from department to 
department and does not reflect on DDS as a whole
1) DDS has taken on board a, proven, recruitment direction where aesthetically 
pleasing staff are recruited on a department basis. The aim of this basis is to 
group employees within a department where they are less likely to be distracted 
by the aesthetics of individual employees and are able to focus on their 
individual accomplishments.
1) The main goal of DDS is to become a market leader within all aspects of the 
Media-space and not rely on any sole aspect of IIP nor performance to garner 
reputational respect. DDS deserves respect by existing.

See how lucky we are?

that my department will not get any fit birds and QA gets them all due to the 
existing fit bird(s) there.. rubbish! :(

What light from yonder 5th floor corner glows?
It is a smile,
A smile like that of the sun when it first kisses the horizon,
And, like the caress of first dawn, all who see that smile feel a warmth that 
comes from that  
same knowledge that angels must feel in the prescence of divine beauty.

Are you beauty? My eyes are unsure, bewildered, blinded..
Perhaps so, or perhaps just beauty enough for this poor soul

Have a good weekend mon petit pois

	Subject
	This is Very Funny
	
	
	
	
	




After every flight, Qantas Australia   pilots fill out a form, called a
"gripesheet," which tells mechanics about problems with the aircraft.

The mechanics correct the problems, document their repairs on the
form, and then pilots review the gripe sheets before the next flight.

Never let it be said that ground crews lack a sense of humor.

Here are some actual maintenance complaints submitted by Qantas' pilots
(marked with a P) and the solutions recorded (marked with an S) by maintenance 
engineers.

By the way Qantas is the only major airline that has never, ever, had an
accident.



P: Left inside main tire almost needs replacement.

S: Almost replaced left inside main tire.

P: Test flight OK, except auto-land very rough.

S: Auto-land not installed on this aircraft.

P: Something loose in cockpit.

S: Something tightened in cockpit.

P: Dead bugs on windshield.

S: Live bugs on back-order.

P: Autopilot in altitude-hold mode produces a 200 feet per minute
descent.

S: Cannot reproduce problem on ground.

P: Evidence of leak on right main landing gear.

S: Evidence removed.

P: DME volume unbelievably loud.

S: DME volume set to more believable level.

P: Friction locks cause throttle levers to stick.

S: That's what friction locks are for.

P: IFF inoperative in OFF mode.

S: IFF always inoperative in OFF mode.

P: Suspected crack in windshield.

S: Suspect you're right.

P: Number 3 engine missing.

S: Engine found on right wing after brief search.

P: Aircraft handles funny.

S: Aircraft warned to straighten up, fly right, and be serious.

P: Target radar hums.

S: Reprogrammed target radar with lyrics.

P: Mouse in cockpit.

S: Cat installed.

And the best one for last.................

P: Noise coming from under instrument panel. Sounds like a midget

pounding on something with a hammer.

S: Took hammer away from midget.

From: Roland Jutai

Subject: Zapper  [SPAM]


Since everyone’s been asking “What’s  that blue device on your side?!?!?!?!”, I 
thought I’d send an email. This way I  can share the benefits of this great 
device with you and your curiosity is also  satisfied. 

 

So a zapper is an approved medical  device in Canadaand they use it post 
surgery  to contain viruses and bacteria. It works by feeding an electric 
current through  your body (a min of 9v is required) with only a positive 
off-set at a low enough  frequency to not affect you but affect the little 
buggers. Every living thing  has a frequency it emits. If you feed that same 
frequency to the living thing  (and in this case the positive offset does not 
matter much, though helps) with a  high enough voltage, they will 
die/disintegrate. The higher the voltage, the  further away from the living 
thing’s frequency you can be… and it will still be  killed. 

 

To illustrate the principle, you  could touch an electric fence with a high 
enough voltage. ;-) Ok, probably not a  good idea! J

 

In any case, the zapper can be used  in two modes:

 

frequency  generation: in this mode you use program cards to sweep through 
certain  frequencies of known pathogens. A frequency list has been put together 
by Dr  Hulde Clarke (use google), but it was not an original idea. Dr. Royal 
Rife  invented the Rife machine in the 1920’s, which worked on the same 
principle,  but a different mechanism (again, use google if want to know more. 
I also  included a little more below *). Now Rife machines were destroyed by 
Rife’s  opponents not long after he made the discovery. ** Anyhow, some of Rife’
s  original frequencies and research is still available. The original design 
is  not. L  
a zapper…  a wave between 1khz and 15khz applied continuously for 9+ minutes 
with only a  positive offset. The wave only reaches pathogens outside the 
bowels or  internal shielded areas. It’s still very good for skin infections or 
anything  in your blood. It will stop a cold/flu if applied at the onset. 
Glutamine (at  over 30-40 gramms a day!!! Your bowels use up a LOTof this 
before it can get to your immune cells) will  help if you’re past the offset 
(the offset is the first ~2 hours of  coughing). 

 

I find the device helps my immune  system a LOT.  This is the reason I use it 
as well as glutamine, arginine,  lysine which modulate the immune system and 
oxygen therapy (which helps keep  down viral and bacterial loads as they are 
mainly anaerobic). Without them I  would not feel too well. This is because my 
immune system is KO from metal  poisoning a few months ago. (That’s for another 
day.) J

 

I’m happy to answer any other  questions you may have. More people should know 
about such things.  J

 

* Rife  Machines:

“Developed in the 1920's by Dr.  Royal Rife, Rife Machine technology is based 
on the M.O.R., or the mortal  oscillatory rate of living organisms.  By 
increasing the intensity of a  frequency which resonated naturally with these 
microbes, Rife increased their  natural oscillations until they distorted and 
disintegrated from structural  stresses. This principle can be illustrated by 
using an intense musical note to  shatter a wine glass: the molecules of the 
glass are already oscillating at some  harmonic (multiple) of that musical 
note; they are in resonance with it. Because  everything else has a different 
resonant frequency, nothing but the glass is  destroyed.” From 
http://www.truerife.com/

 

 

** (Read on only if you’re  interested in my opinion and experience … ) Yes, 
the medical  establishment is all about money primarily as well. This is 
especially true  nowadays where drug companies would rather see you pumped full 
of expensive  drugs, but try every way to stop research on any project that 
might end up in  things that deliver a cure but cannot be patented. Let’s not 
even go into lots  of government officials having (big) shares in drug 
companies and where that  led/leads healthcare, the media in general and us. 
;-) This is why you should  consider supporting truly independent research and 
give government funded  research a miss. Unfortunately, I find most cancer and 
AIDS research  organisations fall into this category and therefore completely 
miss the point!  These conditions don’t have to be deadly if you know what 
research to look at  and take toxic drugs as a very very last resort. You 
should also question  everything the doctors tell you. I find most 
doctors/experts only focus on their  research area and miss the systemic 
effects and drug interactions. It’s very  rare to find a doctor who has a 
wholeistic ;-) approach to things, but there are  some around. Even if they do 
have such an approach, they are bound legally by so  many things that they 
cannot provide you with treatment not supported by the  government. They could 
lose their licence! I experienced it on my own skin where  doctors were happy 
to administer treatment for things they knew would help (or I  demanded) but 
only after I signed legal forms to protect their licence. Of  course this 
becomes rather expensive as the NHS only pays for government  supported 
treatment (nothing wrong with that of course). So do your own  research, ask 
for multiple opinions and take everything you read/doctors tell  you with a 
bucket of salt!!! You’re welcome to disagree of course. I thought  very 
differently about these things just a few short months ago.  :-)

 

Roland

Since everyone’s been asking “What’s  that round device on your front?!?!?!?!”, 
I thought I’d send an email. This way  I can share the benefits of this great 
device with you and your curiosity is  also satisfied. 

 

So a beer belly is an approved  medical device in Canadaand they use it post 
surgery  to contain viruses and bacteria. It works by feeding an excessive 
amount of  lager / bitter through your body (a min of 9 pints a day is 
required) with only  a low enough alcohol percentage to get you hammered and 
affect the little  bugger. One particular living thing has a flavoursome 
frequency it emits. If you  feed that same frequency to the living thing (and 
in this case the 2 kebabs do  not matter much, though helps) with a high enough 
volume, they will  die/disintegrate from the smell. The louder the toot, the 
further away from  living thing’s you can be… and it will still be killed.  

 

To illustrate the principle, you  could eat 15 cans of baked beans 
consecutively. ;-) Ok, probably not a good  idea! J

 

In any case, the belly can be used  in two modes:

 

resting  place for drinks: in this mode you use flat surface area to save the 
hassle of  making your arm get a bit tired. A measurement list has been put 
together by  Dr Al Murray (use google), but it was not an original idea. Dr. 
Morgan  invented the belly table in the 1920’s, which worked on the same 
principle,  but a different mechanism (again, use google if want to know more. 
I also  included a little more below *). Now belly tables were destroyed by 
Morgan’s  opponents not long after he made the discovery. ** Anyhow, some of 
Morgan’s  original frequencies and research is still available, although his 
handwriting  was a little illegible since he was drunk at the time. The 
original design is  not. L  
an excuse  for the phrase “more of me to love”… a wave between 1khz and 15khz 
applied  continuously for 9+ minutes will happen if you tap one side of the 
belly. The  wave only reaches pathogens outside the bowels or internal shielded 
areas.  It’s still very good for skin infections or anything in your blood. It 
will  stop a cold/flu if applied at the onset. Kebabs (at over 30-40 gramms a 
day!!!  Your bowels use up a LOTof this before it  can get to your immune 
cells) will help if you’re past the offset (the offset  is the first ~2 hours 
of puking). 

 

I find the device helps my escapism  from reality a LOT.  This is the reason I  
use it as well as wine, vodka and gin which modulate the immune system and  
burger therapy (which helps keep down viral and bacterial loads as they are  
mainly flame grilled). Without them I would not feel too well. This is because  
my I am a greedy, greedy man. (That’s for another day.) J

 

I’m happy to answer any other  questions you may have. More people should know 
about such things.  J

 

* Belly  tables:

“Developed in the 1920's by Dr.  Morgan, belly table technology is based on the 
M.O.M., or the Morgan oval mound  of living organisms.  By increasing the 
intensity of a lager which  resonated naturally with these microbes, Morgan 
increased their natural  oscillations until they distorted and disintegrated 
from structural stresses.  This principle can be illustrated by necking a pint 
of Guinness, pulling your  top up and looking in the mirror: the molecules of 
the glass are already  oscillating from the shock at losing the liquid so 
quickly; they are in  resonance with it. Because everything else has a 
different resonant frequency,  nothing but the sobriety is destroyed.”

 

Steve

From: Mark Zachary

Hetpopkids,

After failing the world record attempt for longest ever roller-skating
conga line (true), I think we should give this a go. If you're
interested in taking part, let me know, and I'll register ye when I call
up today.


World Record Attempt Coconut Orchestra
======================================
April 23rd is St George's Day, so let's do the obvious and join a
coconut orchestra . Trafalgar Square hosts a celebration of English
comedy, with screenings from 12.30, a coconut rehearsal at 6.30
(register for your complimentary 'nuts before then), followed by an
official world record attempt at 7pm led by the cast of Spamalot . The
aim is to gather more than 1785 coconut-clopping sillies on one
non-asylum site. Once the great unhinged have achieved victory, 'Monty
Python and the Holy Grail' will be shown at 7.30. So to re-cap, on St
George's Day we always look on the bright side of life, bang coconut
halves together and sing. Obvious, really. The only curious thing is how
so foreign a fruit to our climes could possibly signify so much for
British comedy?

The other night I was invited out for a night with "the  boys."
I promised my girlfriend that I would be home by midnight. Well, the  hours
passed and the pint's, whiskey's, etc went down way too  easy.

Around 3 a.m., totally pissed, I headed for home. Just as I got in  the
door, the cuckoo clock in the hall started up and cuckooed three  times.
Quickly realizing my girlfriend would probably wake up, I cuckooed  another
nine times. I was really proud of myself for coming up with such  a
quick-witted solution, in order to escape a possible conflict with  her.

(Even when totally smashed, three cuckoos plus nine cuckoos totals  12
cuckoos = MIDNIGHT!)
The next morning my girlfriend asked me what time  I got in, and I told her
" Midnight." she didn't seem pissed off at  all.

Whew! Got Away with that one !!

Then she said, "We need a new  cuckoo clock."

When I asked her why, she said, "Well, last night our  clock cuckooed three
times, then said, 'Oh. Shit,' cuckooed four more times,  cleared it's
throat, cuckooed another three times, giggled, cuckooed  twice
more, then tripped over the coffee table and  farted."

Labourer  Edition 
This edition of The Office (tm)  is aimed at the casual menial use and consists 
of the following:  

Rusty Filing Cabinet (tm) version  1.0

Chewed Pencil (tm) version 2005

The Tabloid Manual Labourer's Library (TMLL)

page-3 clips of all tabloids for  2003-2005. (Note. Articles supplied on 
seperate 3.5" SD floppy disk, imagery on  15DVDs) 

QA Edition 
This edition of The Office (tm) is aimed at those users  more comfortable with 
stress-testing their Office (tm) 

Interesting Filing Cabinet (tm) version 1.2

Extendy Pencil (tm)  version 2005 (incl. Eraser 1.0)

The Broadsheet  Backissue Library (BBL)

Hyperlinks are provided in the online version to the Stars, funnies and Soduko  
pages that you really do use. 
         NOTE: Articles supplied on seperate single 5.25" floppy,  other

Developer Edition

darker, concealed environments. 

Cool Filing Cabinet (tm) version 2005

Cool Keyboard  (tm)

Hyperlinks are provided in the online version  to the Stars, funnies and Soduko 
pages that you really do use.

------- Comment #3 From Jeremy Jee  2007-06-07 11:44  [reply]  ------- 

Don’t Quit!

When things go wrong, as they sometimes will,
when the road you’re trudging seems all uphill,
When the funds are low and the debts are high,
And you want to smile, but you have to sigh,
When care is pressing you down a bit,
Rest, if you must, but do not quit.

Life is queer with its twists and turns,
As every one of us sometimes learns,
And many a failure turns about,
When he might have won had he stuck it out;
Don’t give up though the pace seems slow—
You may succeed with another blow.

Often the goal is nearer than,
It seems to a faint and faltering man,
Often the struggler has given up,
When he might have captured the victor’s cup,
And he learned too late when the night slipped down,
How close he was to the golden crown.

Success is failure turned inside out—
The silver tint of the clouds of doubt,
And you never can tell how close you are,
It may be near when it seems so far,
So stick to the fight when you’re hardest hit—
It’s when things seem worst that you must not quit.


- Exit instead
